results.name: The seeded register reproduces the exact accepted Riverbend basis
Every seeded handover reports a known state, destination and conversion outcome
A fully allocated destination carries the accepted discount; a partial one does not
A Won opportunity with no bound acceptance cannot be prepared into a submission
Roles and receiving scope are enforced atomically
A stale expected version is refused without changing anything
A return must identify what is missing, who responds and by when
Responsibility cannot be accepted while acceptance evidence is outstanding
A return preserves the submitted revision unchanged
A missing supporting document needs an exact revision and source, not a tick
Requirement outcomes retain their earlier finding and need a reason when not applicable
Correction creates a successor revision and a readable comparison
Acceptance binds the exact revision and does not clear release prerequisites
An accepted handover cannot be accepted twice and rejects a new decision without a submission
A later source change requires renewed acceptance and keeps the original decision
A bound source that changes during review invalidates the submitted revision
An unresolved conversion blocks fulfilment acceptance and names ES-07
An unavailable receiving record blocks acceptance and is stated, not hidden
An original operation replays once and never surfaces under another identity or handover
One obligation is one record and cannot be duplicated or completed twice
A receiving link is prepared once and creates no second record
Withdrawal preserves the submission and records no responsibility
The nine-event responsibility chain is never collapsed
A serialised session validates and round-trips exactly
Money and dates use Australian conventions
